prompt: Use case: identity-preserve narrative restaging. First inputs canonical identity portraits; next room master is only architectural/palette reference; LAST input is prior scene for cast, approved face morphology and exact task content, NOT a pose to preserve. Preserve each canonical face, adult age, hair, eye/nose/jaw proportions and characteristic accessories. Farah lens anatomical LEFT eye; Demir comms anatomical RIGHT ear; Nazari and Mirza have no eyewear. Balanced stylized adult head/body scale, neither oversized heads nor realistic tiny heads. Clean cel-shaded adventure-comic linework, natural supported anatomy, two arms per character. Restage as a candid engineering-bench investigation, not a presenter. Farah sits sideways at a working console, body and chair toward the screen. The camera peers diagonally from the screen side so her canonical three-quarter face and the actual surface are visible. Her eyebrows lift with skeptical disappointment as she notices the blend lost; she underlines the best member row with a stylus in her anatomical right hand while the left hand steadies the notebook beside the console. No held-up tablet, no camera gaze. The console has a compact source-grounded table headed Illustrative comparison: Member 1 MAE0.052; Member 2 MAE0.036; Member 3 MAE0.050; Blend MAE0.041. Highlight only the Member2 row with a subdued sage wash. A small annotation next to the table reads Best member wins this comparison. All labels and rules match the oblique screen plane, naturally legible from the side, never pasted frontally. Other displays off. A plain mug and ordinary blank-backed notes sit on the bench. Muted brass and charcoal engineering bay, no neon. Hands and stylus contact realistic, shoulder and neck alignment natural. Output one full 1536x1024 scene. No text outside genuine work artifacts, no captions, no hero portraits, no camera-facing eye contact or lesson cards.
